use_case: A small regional museum's collection catalog: objects, makers, exhibitions, provenance history and outgoing loans.
organization_name: Wraithmoor Regional Museum of Art & Craft

makers.name: Odalys Marchetti
makers.bio: Painter working primarily in oil, associated with a regional Ashcan-adjacent circle documenting industrial waterfronts. Largely undocumented until a 2004 retrospective at a university gallery.

makers.name: Wendell Achebe-Foss
makers.bio: Sculptor working in welded steel and salvaged industrial parts, active in the postwar British scrap-metal sculpture movement.

makers.name: Junko Ariyoshi
makers.bio: Living textile artist known for indigo-dyed shibori panels that reinterpret traditional techniques at architectural scale.

makers.name: Hollis Vandermeer
makers.bio: Printmaker and WPA-era muralist; several of his public murals were destroyed in the 1970s and survive only in preparatory sketches.

makers.name: Concepcion Lariosa
makers.bio: Sculptor working in narra and molave hardwoods, trained under a santo-carving tradition before moving into abstract forms.

makers.name: Bertram Okonkwo-Hale
makers.bio: Contemporary ceramicist known for large-scale unglazed stoneware vessels referencing brutalist architecture.

makers.name: Astrid Lindqvist-Berg
makers.bio: Photographer whose glass-plate negatives documenting rural depopulation were rediscovered in an estate sale in 1988.

makers.name: Emeric Toth-Varga
makers.bio: Furniture maker and industrial designer who bridged Bauhaus training with mass-market American furniture manufacturing.

makers.name: Ruth Isakssen
makers.bio: Weaver working in traditional Norwegian tapestry techniques adapted to abstract mid-century compositions.

makers.name: Attributed workshop of the Wraithmoor Valley Potters
makers.bio: An unattributed group of early settlement-era potters working in the local red clay tradition; individual makers are not documented.

objects.title: Coalyard at Dusk
objects.description: A dockside coal yard rendered in muted ochres and blue-grays, workers reduced to silhouette against a crane's superstructure. Purchased directly from the artist's estate; one of only four known surviving canvases from her waterfront series.
objects.credit_line: Gift of the Marchetti Family Trust

objects.title: Furnace Fragment No. 4
objects.medium: Welded steel and cast iron fragments
objects.description: Part of a series built from decommissioned foundry parts sourced from a Sheffield scrapyard the artist visited weekly for two years.
objects.credit_line: Purchased with funds from the Regional Arts Endowment

objects.title: Indigo Wall (Study)
objects.description: A preparatory study for the artist's permanent installation at a Kyoto train station, using a resist technique she developed combining arashi and itajime methods.
objects.credit_line: Museum purchase

objects.title: Mill Workers, Preparatory Sketch
objects.description: One of the last surviving studies for the artist's destroyed 1937 post office mural, showing three figures at a loom that do not appear in any surviving photograph of the finished work.
objects.credit_line: Gift of the Federal Art Project Archive

objects.title: Seated Figure in Narra
objects.description: A transitional piece between the artist's early santo-influenced figuration and her later abstract forms; the figure's face is deliberately left unfinished.
objects.credit_line: Gift of Dr. and Mrs. Reynaldo Aquino

objects.title: Monolith Vessel VII
objects.description: Hand-built in sections over eleven weeks, referencing the demolished brutalist car park that stood near the artist's studio.
objects.credit_line: Museum purchase

objects.title: Emptied Village, Series I-VI
objects.medium: Gelatin silver prints from glass-plate negatives
objects.description: Six prints documenting a valley community before its 1930s abandonment; the negatives were found wrapped in newspaper inside a barn wall during a 1988 estate clearance.
objects.credit_line: Gift of the Lindqvist-Berg Estate

objects.title: Bent Plywood Lounge Chair, Prototype
objects.description: An unreleased prototype rejected by the manufacturer for being too expensive to tool; only two prototypes are known to survive.
objects.credit_line: Purchased at auction

objects.title: Fjord Tapestry
objects.description: A large abstract tapestry adapting billedvev technique to a nonrepresentational composition, exhibited once in the artist's lifetime.
objects.credit_line: Gift of the Isakssen Family

objects.title: Red Clay Storage Jar
objects.maker: Attributed workshop of the Wraithmoor Valley Potters
objects.description: Utilitarian storage jar excavated during the 1974 courthouse renovation; part of a cache of eleven vessels of similar form and clay body.
objects.credit_line: Transfer from the County Historical Commission

objects.title: Untitled Steel Study
objects.description: A tabletop maquette believed to be a study for the never-realized public commission 'Foundry Gate.'
objects.credit_line: Purchased with funds from the Regional Arts Endowment

objects.title: Portrait of a Loom Operator
objects.description: One of an edition of thirty; the museum holds impression 4/30, notable for hand-added chalk highlights not present in other known impressions.
objects.credit_line: Gift of the Federal Art Project Archive

objects.title: Abstracted Torso
objects.description: A fully abstract late work, acquired directly from the artist's final solo exhibition before her death.
objects.credit_line: Gift of Dr. and Mrs. Reynaldo Aquino

objects.title: Monolith Vessel III
objects.description: An earlier vessel in the Monolith series, smaller in scale and with visible finger-ridging the artist later smoothed out in subsequent works.
objects.credit_line: Museum purchase

objects.title: Emptied Village, Contact Sheet
objects.description: A working contact sheet showing frames not selected for the final print series, useful for establishing the shoot's actual sequence.
objects.credit_line: Gift of the Lindqvist-Berg Estate

objects.title: Dining Chair, Production Model
objects.description: The production version of the rejected 1949 prototype, released after cost reductions to the tooling process; sold widely through the mid-1950s.
objects.credit_line: Purchased at auction

objects.title: Fjord Tapestry, Design Cartoon
objects.description: The full-scale design drawing used to guide the tapestry's weaving, showing a color palette abandoned in the final piece.
objects.credit_line: Gift of the Isakssen Family

objects.title: Red Clay Pitcher
objects.maker: Attributed workshop of the Wraithmoor Valley Potters
objects.description: From the same courthouse cache as the storage jar, distinguished by a distinctive thumb-pressed handle join.
objects.credit_line: Transfer from the County Historical Commission

objects.title: Indigo Wall (Final Panel Fragment)
objects.description: A fragment retained by the artist from the final installation after water damage required a section to be remade; donated separately from the study.
objects.credit_line: Gift of the artist

objects.title: Coalyard Study, Unfinished
objects.description: An unfinished preparatory study for 'Coalyard at Dusk', abandoned mid-composition and useful for understanding the artist's underpainting method.
objects.credit_line: Gift of the Marchetti Family Trust

exhibitions.title: Waterfronts and Foundries: Industry in Regional Art, 1900-1970
exhibitions.description: A survey pairing Marchetti's waterfront paintings with Achebe-Foss's foundry-sourced sculpture, tracing how regional artists represented industrial decline across seven decades.

exhibitions.title: Rediscovered: The Lindqvist-Berg Negatives
exhibitions.description: The first public showing of the full Lindqvist-Berg negative archive since its 1988 discovery, including several prints never before exhibited.

exhibitions.title: Hand and Loom: Textile Traditions Reworked
exhibitions.description: Isakssen's tapestries shown alongside Ariyoshi's shibori panels, examining how two makers a generation and a continent apart reinterpreted inherited textile technique.

exhibitions.title: The Unfinished Object
exhibitions.description: A small gallery of unfinished, abandoned, or preparatory works from the permanent collection, including studies by Marchetti, Vandermeer, and the Isakssen cartoon.

exhibitions.title: Molded and Manufactured: Toth-Varga's Furniture
exhibitions.description: A design-history exhibition tracing a single chair from rejected prototype to mass-market production, using the museum's rare surviving prototype as its centerpiece.

exhibitions.title: Local Clay: Ten Thousand Years of the Wraithmoor Valley
exhibitions.description: A long-running regional archaeology and craft exhibition connecting the courthouse cache pottery to contemporary work by Okonkwo-Hale.
